title: Choose Squadup's visual world
question: The roll assigned Departures. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Departures
options.lineage: Boarding passes and split-flap departure boards
options.thesis: Every hangout is a departure: you hold a pass, every car is a flight, and status flips like a departure board.
options.viewport: Top: your boarding pass for the hangout (venue, date, your car and seat, pickup time). Below: a Needs-you board and a live rides board whose status cells flip (ON TIME, ON THE WAY, OUTSIDE). Standard bottom tab bar.
options.risk: Can tip into airline cosplay if the pass grows beyond one card; the shell must stay a normal app.

raised.raise: One strict tonal ramp: every neutral is a step of the same violet-black, no ad-hoc greys.
One rule weight everywhere; states are marks: filled = yours, struck = done or declined.
What's yours is ringed, like a circled entry, so your car, your vote and your task are findable at a glance.
Density courage on Home: real facts packed in ruled modules, no inflated empty cards.
Everything gets a code: cars and polls carry short codes (CAR A1, POLL 03) used consistently.
Times are set right-aligned in tabular figures, so the schedule and pickups scan like a timetable.

options.label: Gig Ticket
options.lineage: Gig tickets, stubs and festival wristbands
options.thesis: The hangout as a gig: your ticket on Home, requests arrive as stubs you tear to accept.
options.viewport: Top: a big gig ticket with the date as the headline and the venue under it. Below: request stubs (Accept / Decline) and your to-dos. Standard bottom tab bar.
options.risk: Event apps often use ticket motifs, so this is the more familiar choice of the two.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets over a tonal zone ramp.
options.viewport: Stacked translucent sheets, hatching marks conflicts.
options.risk: Teens don't know darkroom cards; hatching hides simple states.
options.case: Loses both: no audience recognition, and hatch-coded state slows a phone glance.
options.kept: One strict tonal ramp for every neutral.

options.label: Centre-rail Reference
options.thesis: Two columns twinned round a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with a keyed centre rail.
options.risk: A book page on a phone at night; wrong energy for a hangout.
options.case: Loses both: bookish, and two columns don't fit a phone task.
options.kept: One rule weight; states as printed marks.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-size cells keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid with circled picks.
options.risk: Niche; a squad has 5 to 15 people, not thousands of cells.
options.case: Loses both: niche recognition, and the grid's scale doesn't match a small group.
options.kept: Yours is ringed, like a circled entry.

options.label: High-density Web
options.thesis: Boxed modules packed edge to edge with red tabs.
options.viewport: A mosaic of tiny boxed modules.
options.risk: Too small to read on a phone in a moving car.
options.case: Loses both: white-and-red breaks the brand palette, and tiny type hurts the task.
options.kept: Density courage: no inflated empty cards.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry on matte black.
options.viewport: A catalog number as the only headline.
options.risk: Colour codes replace words, which hides who is in which car.
options.case: Loses both: coded labels fight clarity, and the reference is lost on teens.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Side A / side B tracklists ruled in ballpoint.
options.viewport: A folded card with timed tracklists.
options.risk: Light paper ground breaks the dark brand; handwriting slows reading.
options.case: Loses both: off-palette, and the A/B split has no product meaning.
options.kept: Right-aligned tabular times, like a timetable.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark mobile app in the brand colours, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Header, a summary card, a to-do list, standard bottom tabs.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other app, which is what the team asked to avoid.
